title: Young adult stroke (<50): extended workup
keyNumbers: Confirmed APS: Warfarin is reasonable; target INR 2–3 over >3
Protein C, protein S, antithrombin, factor VIII: Defer or repeat ≥4–6 weeks after stroke; factor VIII up to 6 months (Kleindorfer)
Age 18–60, nonlacunar cryptogenic stroke, PFO: Closure decision by PFO features — see esus-antithrombotic
consultQuestion: Stroke in a young adult — what beyond the standard workup?
keyHistory: Personal or family history of VTE, miscarriage, early stroke
Migraine with aura, oral contraceptives/estrogen, pregnancy or postpartum
Neck trauma, recent infection, HIV/syphilis risk
Systemic symptoms: rash, arthritis, livedo, weight loss
Hearing loss, renal disease, neuropathic pain (genetic syndromes)
redFlags: Headache with stroke-like deficits (dissection, RCVS, CVT)

clues: Neck pain or headache, Horner, preceding trauma
Cortical infarct, no other cause, Valsalva at onset, DVT
Prior VTE or pregnancy loss, livedo, thrombocytopenia
Recurrent thunderclap headache, postpartum, vasoactive drugs
Headache, seizures, hemorrhagic infarcts not respecting arterial territories
Multifocal infarcts, abnormal vessel imaging, CSF pleocytosis

differential.dx: Genetic: CADASIL, Fabry, MELAS, sickle cell disease
clues: Family history, migraine, white-matter disease, systemic features

workup.test: Standard stroke etiology workup: MRI brain, vessel imaging, ECG and telemetry, echo, routine stroke labs
CTA or MRA head and neck (dissection, vasculopathy)
notes: MRI with fat-saturated T1 neck if dissection suspected

workup.test: TTE with agitated saline; TEE if negative and suspicion remains
Pregnancy test (people who can become pregnant)

indication: Cryptogenic stroke, prior VTE or pregnancy loss
notes: Lupus anticoagulant testing is discouraged on anticoagulation (false positives and negatives); DOAC removal or alternate assays only with lab input (ISTH 2024)

workup.test: Protein C, protein S, antithrombin, factor VIII
notes: Defer or repeat ≥4–6 weeks after stroke; factor VIII up to 6 months (Kleindorfer)

indication: Venous thrombosis, PFO with suspected paradoxical embolism

decisionRules.recommendation: Targeted tests: hypercoagulable state, blood/CSF infection, infections causing CNS vasculitis (e.g., HIV, syphilis), drug use (cocaine, amphetamines), systemic inflammation markers, genetic tests for inherited stroke diseases

decisionRules.condition: Isolated antiphospholipid antibody, APS criteria not met

decisionRules.recommendation: Warfarin is reasonable; target INR 2–3 over >3
No rivaroxaban — excess thrombosis vs warfarin

decisionRules.condition: Inherited thrombophilia found, no other thrombotic history, cryptogenic stroke

decisionRules.recommendation: Closure decision by PFO features — see esus-antithrombotic

disposition: Hematology referral for confirmed thrombophilia or APS
PFO heart team referral when criteria met
institutionVaries: Send-out thrombophilia panel contents and turnaround
pearls: Acute-phase protein C/S/antithrombin levels are unreliable — testing too early creates false positives (Kleindorfer)
Thrombophilia testing rarely changes default antiplatelet therapy unless it shows APS or venous thrombosis (Kleindorfer supportive text)
